chapter: Youth, Storyville and the bands he heard
title: Why he took up music at 14, his father's work and dislike of jitney dances
summary: He wanted to play after hearing music at 14 and worked in a blacksmith shop; his father delivered wholesale meat; he played for love, not money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: that's what I was just telling you plenty of times. And some of these people, you never know their name. They died. Yeah. Never know their name. Did they, did you have a nickname too? No, I never had a nickname. Well, they called me instead of Peter, kind of people called me Pete. Yeah. And that was the closest thing for a nickname. Why did you want to play music in there? Well, like I just told you, I used to listen to this music on Saturday night around the corner from my house. And I was a boy, but oh, I guess I must have been about 14 years old. And I just like to, thought I'd like to be one of them fellas doing that. And so I started to try. Did you have any trouble getting money together, about a while? Well, no, I worked today. You worked on? No, I was a boy about 14, but I was working. Oh, yeah. People don't work like that no more. No. They've got to be 18 before they work, and that's a good thing in a way, and it's a bad thing,
because it makes plenty of people lazy. Did you like to work when you were 14? Yeah, I like to work. I used to go to work with a good heart. And what kind of work were you doing?

Well, I was helping me in a blacksmith shop. First, I was in a drug school, getting 50 cents a day, 50 cents a week to go deliver orders of the druggish. What did your parents do, your father and your money? Well, my father drove a team of horses. Well, they delivered a delivery wagon. I'll tell you what, like this Wilson and Company or Homo people. Well, he worked for a company of that sort, but sold wholesale meats. I mean, deliver. We can stop it. He's consigned. I used to deliver this meat at night. What was his name? His name was Peter Lacazzo. I heard of Meat Man's feet. That's a wreck. No, that's something different.
Yeah, that's something different. That's something different. So, in other words, you didn't go into your father's business?

No. No, I went, tell you what happened. I went to that place where he worked one day, and I tried to walk around in there, and it was very slippery there. You know, it kept bloody and all kind of stuff on the floor. The floor was an asphalt pavement floor, very slippery. And somebody, some of the people worked there, threw a piece at me, hit me on the bottom of my foot, knocked me down, put a hump on my face. You didn't like that? I didn't go back no more. Go back over there no more. They could keep that. Decided for another day. Yeah, get some other kind of job. They could keep that.
In other words, you didn't play music because you needed a money then?
No. No, just because I loved it. I see myself go on jobs where somebody else is working and take over for them just to be doing it. Oh, yeah.
Yeah, I did that several times. In other words, you weren't that interested in playing every night then? No, no, no. And you didn't like the jitner dance?
No, no, I didn't like that because you had a way too steady. I never got a chance to take a breath.
